attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Keeps his hedges ('arguably', 'if I followed correctly', 'if the measures are the same') and his 'in November'. Neither adds to nor drops from what he committed to.

contract.note: The contract keeps his own condition that the measures match and does not turn the hedged ranking into a flat assertion. Reading November as Nov 2024 is the ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Nov 2024 MIT preprint reports 61.9%, but for an ensemble on public validation tasks. This backs only his approximate 61% figure, not the ranking.
ARC Prize's April 2025 o3 results use semi-private tasks, unlike the paper's public validation split. So his 'measures are the same' condition is not met.

reviews.rationale: The 61% recollection roughly holds (61.9%, ensemble, public split). But his claim that it beat o3 is explicitly conditional on matching measures, and it is hedged. The evidence shows the splits differ (public vs semi-private), so the antecedent fails and the comparison isn't scored. 'Not much different' has no threshold.
